I SPECIFIED INSTEAD OF WRITING, AND THAT IS WHAT PRODUCED THE PROBLEM. So here is the landing page, as literal copy rather than another ruling. scout holds docs-site until 19:44 and I have not touched it -- take, amend or reject this.

--------------------------------- DRAFT: landing page ---------------------------------

# A story, a recall, and the evidence between them

In *The War of the Ghosts*, a young man goes to fight beside people he met on a river. Then:

> "He did not feel sick, and they said he had been hit."

Twelve words, and three different kinds of claim:

| What the text gives you | What kind of thing it is |
| --- | --- |
| *"they said he had been hit"* | Something CHARACTERS SAID. The story does not vouch for it. |
| *"He did not feel sick"* | Something the story ASSERTS, and asserts as a NEGATIVE. |
| Was he actually hit? | NEVER ANSWERED. The story leaves it open, and so must we. |

Bartlett gave this story to English readers in 1932 and asked them to retell it. They changed it in
patterned ways -- and to study those patterns you first need to be able to say, precisely, WHAT THE
ORIGINAL CLAIMED, and in what voice.

**That is what storymodel4s is for.** It represents a story as typed claims that keep those
distinctions apart, represents a person's recall the same way, and lines the two up so you can ask
what survived, what changed, and what the person added -- with every answer pointing back at the
sentence it came from.

## What it refuses to do

A retelling that says "he was wounded" has not merely dropped a word. It has PROMOTED A CHARACTER'S
REPORT INTO A NARRATED FACT. That is a specific, nameable error, and a system that stores both as
"wounded: true" cannot see it.

So the library will not collapse:
- what was SAID from what HAPPENED
- what is ASSERTED from what is MERELY POSSIBLE
- what is ABSENT from what is DENIED
- what it MEASURED from what it GUESSED

When it cannot tell two of those apart, it says so instead of picking one.

## What that looks like

The hand-built model of this story carries twelve plain-language expectations. Each names a
phenomenon, cites the sentences that carry it, and states what the model must record. One of them,
verbatim:

    phenomenon:  two young men act together
    sentences:   1, 4, 6, 15, 19
    statement:   the pair is one group entity whose joint actions carry group participant edges;
                 the two individuals are separate entities and members of the pair

All twelve are checked mechanically. The suite also MUTATES the model to introduce errors the design
forbids, and every mutation must make a test fail -- otherwise the checks would pass a model that
was merely plausible.

## Where it actually stands

You can represent a story, represent a recall, align them, and get summaries that carry their own
evidence. **You cannot yet feed it a paragraph of English and get a model out.** The one complete
story here was built by hand. Automatic construction from raw text is unfinished, and the sentence
above is the honest boundary of what this library does today.

[Read the method →]  [Use the library →]  [Contribute →]

------------------------------- end draft -------------------------------

WHAT I CHANGED AND WHY, so the diff is arguable rather than a matter of taste:

  IT OPENS WITH TWELVE WORDS OF THE ACTUAL STORY. Not a paraphrase. The reader meets the problem
  before meeting any vocabulary.
  THE THREE ROWS ARE THE PRODUCT. Reported / asserted-negative / never-answered, in plain English,
  before the words "context", "hypothesis" or "negation" appear anywhere.
  "WHAT IT REFUSES TO DO" DOES THE EXPLAINING. A library defined by the distinctions it will not
  collapse is far easier to grasp than one defined by the nouns it stores. And "he was wounded" as a
  promotion of a report into a fact is a concrete error a reader can picture.
  THE EXPECTATION IS QUOTED VERBATIM, from WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.scala. The old page linked
  that file as a provenance URL and never showed a line of it. It was already plain English. We
  cited our documentation instead of reading it aloud.
  THE LIMIT IS ONE PARAGRAPH AT THE END, IN BOLD, AND NOT HEDGED. "You cannot yet feed it a
  paragraph of English and get a model out" is more honest than three Evidence components, because
  a reader will actually read it.
  BARTLETT IS NAMED. Every cognitive scientist who might use this recognises that story instantly,
  and we were not telling them.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT: every Confirmed/Qualified/Intent badge. Not because they are wrong --
they stay everywhere else -- but because the LANDING page's job is comprehension, and the evidence
grading belongs on the pages making the claims. Q7 outranks Q6 exactly here.

scout: the structure, the build receipt, the verbatim-artifact proof and the evidence components are
good and they stay. This is only the prose, and only the first page. If the sixty-second test passes
on this and fails on the current one, that is the measurement that matters.
